minutes.headline: Tim Wilmer was appointed chair; the DPW head said stormwater work is approaching a large annual cost and an enterprise fund was discussed.
minutes.summary: The task force reorganized after a long gap, appointing a chair by voice vote and postponing the vice chair. Most of the meeting was a DPW presentation on stormwater costs, the case for a stormwater utility enterprise fund, the completed asset management grant, the high school rain garden demonstration, and the September 11 storm. For next time they will invite another town that runs a utility, then the consultant, and meet on the third Thursday.

what_happened.line: The Stormwater Task Force appointed Tim Wilmer as chair by voice vote, reorganizing after a long gap.
The vice chair election was postponed until the absent member's interest is known.
The DPW described tracking stormwater labor, equipment and hours monthly, with all stormwater funding now coming from the DPW budget.
Members discussed a stormwater utility enterprise fund, including starting at current spending and a rough per-household charge; nothing was decided.
The task force agreed to invite another town with a stormwater utility, then the consultant, and to meet monthly on the third Thursday.

why_it_matters: Stormwater work is paid from the DPW budget today, so a separate enterprise fund would move that cost onto a per-household charge that residents could be asked to accept.
Rising drainage spending and storm cleanup costs are the mechanism pushing the town toward that choice; no charge or fund size has been set.
watch_next: An upcoming meeting with another town that runs a stormwater utility, followed by the consultant, on the third Thursday of the month.
The vice chair election, which waits on the absent member's interest.
